claims.text: The driver's own GPS trace places him no closer than 780 metres to the pickup pin at any point in the trip: the closest of his 98 fixes is 779.93 m from the pin, against a STANDARD arrival radius of 50 m. On the POL-NS-02 test there is not one qualifying in-radius fix anywhere in the window preceding the 08:09:40 cancellation, so the driver never arrived at the pickup point and POL-NS-01 limb (b) fails. The rider is entitled to a full refund of the $4.00 fee.

POL-NS-01 makes the fee chargeable only if all four conditions hold, and two of them fail here. Limb (b) fails because the driver's trace never enters the 50 m pickup geofence, and limb (c) fails independently because the longest qualifying in-geofence run is 0 seconds and there are 0 qualifying fixes, against the 300 second minimum dwell for STANDARD. The 'arrived' event and the RIDER_NO_SHOW cancellation code on their own satisfy nothing: with limbs (b) and (c) gone, the $4.00 cancellation fee is not chargeable under POL-NS-01 and the case falls to be decided under the refund clauses.

The 'arrived' event timestamped 08:02:14 is a false arrival marker. POL-NS-05 catches a marker set at a moment when the trace places the driver more than 300 m from the pin, and every one of the driver's 98 fixes lies 779.93 m or further away, so the marker is false and cannot start the waiting clock. Because no qualifying in-geofence fix exists anywhere in the trip, POL-NS-05(ii) applies squarely: the fee is refunded in full, no driver compensation is payable, and the trip should be recorded as a false-arrival event against the driver in the ruling's referrals list.

Even taking the platform's arrival marker entirely at face value, the effective in-geofence dwell is zero: the trace yields 0 in-geofence runs with a longest run of 0.0 seconds, against the 300 second minimum for STANDARD. Under POL-NS-06 the fee is therefore not chargeable and is refunded to the rider in full, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not she responded to messages.

There is no advisory in this record that could permit separate in-geofence intervals to be summed under POL-NS-06(i). EV-ADVIS-00201-01 is MISSING, carries weight 0.0 and the issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT; I cite the absence itself, and I disclose that this artifact is at zero weight and carries no fact. Nothing here permits accumulation of dwell - and in any event there is nothing to accumulate, because the driver's trace shows zero in-geofence intervals.

The rider did exactly what POL-NS-04 requires. At 08:05:33, inside the waiting window, she sent 'hello? i dont see any car at 118' - a coordinating message identifying her block and stating that she cannot see the vehicle, which satisfies limb (a). Limb (b) is satisfied because the driver neither posted a reply within 120 seconds nor placed any in-app call before terminating the trip: the chat's last message is hers at 08:05:33 and trip_record.in_app_calls is empty, with termination at 08:09:40. Limb (c) is satisfied because her device sat within 24.93 m of the pin across all 122 qualifying rider fixes, far inside the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius. All three limbs hold, so the fee is refunded in full and no driver compensation is payable.

No wrong-entrance or pin-ambiguity analysis can sustain this charge. POL-NS-03 applies only where the driver was stationary for the required dwell outside the arrival radius but within 400 m of the pickup pin; the driver's closest approach was 779.93 m, roughly twice that ceiling, so the 400 m test is decisive on distance alone and it is not met. The pickup pin's venue_id (VEN-RIVERVALE-DR) does not help the driver either, because nothing in the trace establishes any venue at which he stopped; where the point is not established, the distance test governs alone.

None of the POL-NS-09 escalation triggers is engaged, so this case should be decided now with a full refund rather than put on hold. The anti-farming check reads driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d = 3 against driver_profile.completed_trips_30d = 96, i.e. 3.1%, below both the 4-termination and 0.08 thresholds in POL-NS-07, so limb (d) does not fire; rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 0 and both parties' disputes_with_counterparty_90d are 0, so limb (c) does not fire; no two admissible artifacts contradict each other on arrival, dwell or rider presence; and the deciding facts rest on artifacts at weight 1.0, the only sub-1.0 artifact being the MISSING advisory at 0.0 on which no positive fact rests. Under POL-NS-09 the disputed fee is held only if a trigger fires, and none does; POL-GEN-02 caps confidence at the weight of the artifacts carrying the deciding fact, which is 1.0.

No POL-NS-08 policy-level impairment attaches to the artifacts carrying these findings, so no lower confidence cap and no mandatory escalation arises from evidence integrity. There is no clock skew (the 08:02:14 arrival event falls inside the trace window, and trip record and trace agree that the trip terminated at 08:09:40); no trace defect (100% coverage, 10 second sampling, no gaps, 98 fixes, and the rider track is present); no chat defect (2 messages match trip_record.chat_message_count of 2); and no fare defect ($4.00 reconciles with the fee schedule for STANDARD/RYDE_X). The findings therefore survive at full weight and the full refund is available on this record.

The contested sum is exactly the fee charged, so a full refund leaves the rider carrying none of the disputed charge. EV-FARE-00201 shows one $4.00 cancellation fee, charged and not refunded (payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00), and $4.00 is what the fee_schedule resolution rule produces for this trip: the STANDARD zone-class fee and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee are both $4.00, so the greater of the two is $4.00. Under POL-GEN-03 a FULL_REFUND returns the whole contested amount to the filing party, who here is the rider.

claims.text: The two admissible artifacts in this bundle are in direct conflict about whether the driver was ever at the pickup pin, and both carry full weight. EV-TRIP-00201 records an 'arrived' event at 08:02:14, a wait_time_min of 7.4, and a driver cancellation at 08:09:40 coded RIDER_NO_SHOW — on the platform's own trip record the driver stood at Blk 118 Rivervale Drive for over seven minutes. EV-GPS-00201 says the opposite: across 98 fixes at 100% coverage in the same window, derived.driver_track.min_distance_m is 779.93 m and mean_distance_m is 1177.11 m, so the driver never came within three-quarters of a kilometre of the pin. One of the two artifacts is wrong about the arrival, and no arithmetic in the bundle reconciles them.

A conflict of exactly this shape is what POL-NS-09(b) sends to a human reviewer: two admissible artifacts contradicting each other directly on arrival and dwell, one asserting a completed seven-minute wait and the other asserting the driver was never within 780 m of the pin. The rider will press POL-NS-05, which makes the arrival marker false where the trace puts the driver more than 300 m out at the marker timestamp, and the driver accepts that POL-NS-05 is the clause that governs if the judge holds it applies — but applying it requires a finding that the platform's own recorded arrival event is false, and that finding should be made by a reviewer holding both briefs and the admissibility report, not issued by the automated pipeline against the driver. Escalation is terminal under POL-GEN-03: the disputed $4.00 is held rather than collected or refunded while that single question is settled. The driver seeks no POL-NS-07 compensation out of a fee whose chargeability is itself unresolved, and asks for no more than the hold.

POL-NS-07's anti-farming gate does not trip on this driver, and his profile cannot be used to escalate the case as an abuse pattern under POL-NS-09(d). EV-DPROF-00201 records no_show_terminations_30d of 3 against completed_trips_30d of 96 — a rate of 3.1%, below the four-termination count limb and below the 0.08 ratio limb, so compensation could not be withheld on that ground even if the fee survived. On the rider's side EV-RPROF-00201 records no_show_disputes_30d of 0, so neither half of limb (d) fires. Whatever this case turns on, it does not turn on a farming pattern on either side.

POL-NS-09(c) is not engaged either: EV-RPROF-00201 and EV-DPROF-00201 both record disputes_with_counterparty_90d of 0, so there is no trail of repeated no-show disputes between this rider and this driver to escalate on. The remaining profile numbers — the driver's 4.38 rating, 0.14 cancellation_rate and lifetime prior_no_show_flags of 3, the rider's 890 lifetime_trips and 1 prior_disputes_upheld — are CONTEXT ONLY under POL-GEN-01 and may not carry any finding against either party here; in particular the lifetime prior_no_show_flags counter is not the trailing-30-day figure POL-NS-07 reads, and substituting one for the other is forbidden.

The arithmetic of the charge is not in dispute and it checks out. EV-FARE-00201 itemises a $4.00 cancellation fee against a STANDARD zone-class fee of $4.00 and a RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee of $4.00, so the fee_schedule resolution rule — the greater of the two dimensions — is satisfied and the reconciliation difference is 0.00. POL-NS-08(d) therefore does not fire on this bundle and no impairment attaches to the fare artifact. If the fee ultimately falls, it falls on the arrival question, not on the amount charged or on its reconciliation.

The driver does not put the wrong-entrance route under POL-NS-03 in play, and the judge should not be asked to run it. The whole test in that clause is a 400 m ceiling measured from trip_record.pickup, and the driver's own trace puts his closest approach at 779.93 m — roughly twice the ceiling. No venue_id match is asserted, because the trace carries no driver-side venue_id and the point is therefore not established either way, and the driver claims neither the refund allocation of POL-NS-03 nor the 50 percent pin-ambiguity goodwill of POL-NS-03(ii). On this record the driver's evidence shows a location failure; it does not show a wrong-face-of-the-venue case.

ruling.explanation:
The $4.00 no-show cancellation fee charged for trip TRP-00201 does not stand. It is refunded to the rider in full, and no driver compensation is payable.

Why, on the driver's own evidence: EV-GPS-00201 (weight 1.0, 100% coverage, 10-second sampling, 98 fixes across the whole window) places the driver no closer than 779.93 m from the pickup pin at Blk 118 Rivervale Drive, with a mean distance of 1,177.11 m. The STANDARD arrival radius is 50 m, so there is not one qualifying in-geofence fix anywhere in the trip. Under POL-NS-02 the driver never arrived and POL-NS-01 limb (b) fails. Limb (c) fails independently: the longest qualifying in-geofence run is 0 seconds against the 300-second STANDARD minimum. With (b) and (c) gone, the $4.00 fee is not chargeable under POL-NS-01, and it is refunded under POL-NS-06 as well (effective in-geofence dwell 0 seconds, short of the 300-second minimum).

The trip record's 'arrived' event at 08:02:14 (EV-TRIP-00201) does not rescue the charge. Under POL-NS-05 a marker set when the trace puts the driver more than 300 m from the pin is FALSE; every one of the 98 fixes is 779.93 m or further out, so the marker is false and does not start the waiting clock. Recomputed from the first qualifying in-geofence fix there is none, so POL-NS-05(ii) applies: full refund, no compensation, and the trip is recorded against the driver as a false-arrival event (see referrals).

Independently, POL-NS-04 is satisfied: the rider sent a locating message ('hello? i dont see any car at 118') at 08:05:33, the driver neither replied within 120 seconds nor made any in-app call before terminating at 08:09:40, and the rider's device stayed within 24.93 m of the pin across all 122 fixes, far inside the 100 m STANDARD presence radius. That clause also yields a full refund with no driver compensation.

The driver's argument that POL-NS-09(b) requires a human escalation is not accepted. Limb (b) fires only where two admissible artifacts contradict each other on arrival, dwell or rider presence 'and no clause resolves the conflict'. Here POL-NS-05 is the clause that resolves it: it declares the arrived marker false and recomputes the waiting clock from the geofence test, which is exactly what POL-NS-02 and POL-NS-01(b) make the definitive measure of arrival. There is therefore no unresolved contradiction, and the case is decided now rather than held. The other escalation limbs are also clear: no POL-NS-08 impairment attaches to the deciding artifacts (the 08:02:14 arrival event falls inside the trace window and both records agree the trip terminated at 08:09:40; the trace has no gaps, 98 fixes and the rider track present; the chat log's 2 messages match trip_record.chat_message_count of 2; and the $4.00 fee reconciles with the fee schedule), both parties' disputes_with_counterparty_90d are 0, the driver's no_show_terminations_30d is 3 against 96 completed trips (3.1%), and the rider's no_show_disputes_30d is 0. The remaining profile numbers (rating, cancellation_rate, lifetime_trips, prior_disputes_upheld, prior_no_show_flags) are context only under POL-GEN-01 and carry no finding.

POL-NS-03 (wrong entrance / pin ambiguity) does not apply: that clause is limited to a driver stationary within 400 m of the pin, and the driver's closest approach was 779.93 m, roughly twice the ceiling. No refund allocation under POL-NS-03 and no 50 percent pin-ambiguity goodwill arise, and the driver claims neither.

Figures used, from the money block: one cancellation fee of $4.00 (EV-FARE-00201), being the greater of the STANDARD zone-class fee ($4.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee ($4.00), charged and not refunded (payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00). The ruling moves SGD 4.00, returning the whole contested amount to the filing rider.

Independently, the longest qualifying in-geofence run is 0.0 seconds and the qualifying fix count is 0, against the 300-second minimum dwell for STANDARD, so POL-NS-01 limb (c) also fails.

Because no qualifying in-geofence fix exists anywhere in the trip, the 'arrived' event at 08:02:14 is a false arrival marker under POL-NS-05 — every fix places the driver more than 300 m out — and POL-NS-05(ii) applies squarely: the fee is refunded in full, no compensation is payable, and the false arrival is recorded against the driver in the referrals below. POL-NS-06 gives the same result on the effective dwell of 0.0 seconds against the 300-second minimum. ledger.claim: The driver's own GPS trace places him no closer than 780 metres to the pickup pin at any point in the trip: the closest of his 98 fixes is 779.93 m from the pin, against a STANDARD arrival radius of 50 m. On the POL-NS-02 test there is not one qualifying in-radius fix anywhere in the window preceding the 08:09:40 cancellation, so the driver never arrived at the pickup point and POL-NS-01 limb (b) fails. The rider is entitled to a full refund of the $4.00 fee.

POL-NS-01 makes the fee chargeable only if all four conditions hold, and two of them fail here. Limb (b) fails because the driver's trace never enters the 50 m pickup geofence, and limb (c) fails independently because the longest qualifying in-geofence run is 0 seconds and there are 0 qualifying fixes, against the 300 second minimum dwell for STANDARD. The 'arrived' event and the RIDER_NO_SHOW cancellation code on their own satisfy nothing: with limbs (b) and (c) gone, the $4.00 cancellation fee is not chargeable under POL-NS-01 and the case falls to be decided under the refund clauses.

The 'arrived' event timestamped 08:02:14 is a false arrival marker. POL-NS-05 catches a marker set at a moment when the trace places the driver more than 300 m from the pin, and every one of the driver's 98 fixes lies 779.93 m or further away, so the marker is false and cannot start the waiting clock. Because no qualifying in-geofence fix exists anywhere in the trip, POL-NS-05(ii) applies squarely: the fee is refunded in full, no driver compensation is payable, and the trip should be recorded as a false-arrival event against the driver in the ruling's referrals list.

Even taking the platform's arrival marker entirely at face value, the effective in-geofence dwell is zero: the trace yields 0 in-geofence runs with a longest run of 0.0 seconds, against the 300 second minimum for STANDARD. Under POL-NS-06 the fee is therefore not chargeable and is refunded to the rider in full, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not she responded to messages.

There is no advisory in this record that could permit separate in-geofence intervals to be summed under POL-NS-06(i). EV-ADVIS-00201-01 is MISSING, carries weight 0.0 and the issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT; I cite the absence itself, and I disclose that this artifact is at zero weight and carries no fact. Nothing here permits accumulation of dwell - and in any event there is nothing to accumulate, because the driver's trace shows zero in-geofence intervals.

The rider did exactly what POL-NS-04 requires. At 08:05:33, inside the waiting window, she sent 'hello? i dont see any car at 118' - a coordinating message identifying her block and stating that she cannot see the vehicle, which satisfies limb (a). Limb (b) is satisfied because the driver neither posted a reply within 120 seconds nor placed any in-app call before terminating the trip: the chat's last message is hers at 08:05:33 and trip_record.in_app_calls is empty, with termination at 08:09:40. Limb (c) is satisfied because her device sat within 24.93 m of the pin across all 122 qualifying rider fixes, far inside the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius. All three limbs hold, so the fee is refunded in full and no driver compensation is payable.

No wrong-entrance or pin-ambiguity analysis can sustain this charge. POL-NS-03 applies only where the driver was stationary for the required dwell outside the arrival radius but within 400 m of the pickup pin; the driver's closest approach was 779.93 m, roughly twice that ceiling, so the 400 m test is decisive on distance alone and it is not met. The pickup pin's venue_id (VEN-RIVERVALE-DR) does not help the driver either, because nothing in the trace establishes any venue at which he stopped; where the point is not established, the distance test governs alone.

ledger.claim: No POL-NS-08 policy-level impairment attaches to the artifacts carrying these findings, so no lower confidence cap and no mandatory escalation arises from evidence integrity.
